mcq.question: Tangent PQ at P to a circle of radius 5 cm meets line through centre at Q with OQ = 13 cm. Length PQ is:
From an external point, the number of tangents to a circle is:
mcq.explanation: Case 3 in NCERT 10.3 — exactly two tangents.

mcq.question: Radius to point of contact of a tangent is:

assertion_reason.assertion: Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.
assertion_reason.reason: ΔOQP ≅ ΔORP by RHS, so PQ = PR.
assertion_reason.explanation: Theorem 10.2 — both assertion and reason true.

vsa.question: Radius 7 cm, tangent from point 25 cm from centre. Find tangent length.
How many tangents can be drawn from a point lying on the circle?

sa.question: Prove that tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter are parallel.
sa.model_answer: Each tangent ⊥ radius at contact; radii along diameter ⇒ both tangents ⊥ same line ⇒ parallel.

sa.question: Chord of larger circle touches smaller concentric circle. Prove chord is bisected at point of contact.
sa.model_answer: OP ⊥ chord AB at P ⇒ P bisects AB (perpendicular from centre bisects chord).

la.question: Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
la.model_answer: Standard NCERT proof by contradiction using shortest distance from centre to line.

la.question: From external point P, tangents PA and PB are drawn. Prove PA = PB.
la.model_answer: Join OA, OB, OP. ΔOAP ≅ ΔOBP (RHS) ⇒ PA = PB.

la.question: Two tangents TP and TQ from external T make ∠PTQ = 60°. Prove ∠PTQ = 2 ∠OPT.
la.model_answer: TP = TQ ⇒ isosceles; use ∠OPT = 90° and angle chase to get ∠PTQ = 2∠OPT.
